children: Ingenia Communities has agreed to open its books to suitor Warburg Pincus, but management seems to continue to prefer a planned acquisition of Australia-listed Peet, says Citi. Warburg Pincus recently raised its offer for Ingenia to A$5.25/share. That brings it into line with Citi's assessment that Ingenia investors are looking for a bid in a A$5.25-A$5.50/share range. Announcing that it would let Warburg Pincus carry out due diligence, Ingenia said it hasn't determined whether the latest offer is superior to the deal whereby Ingenia acquires Peet. Ingenia also said it hasn't indicated that it intends to recommend the Warburg Pincus offer to its shareholders. Citi retains a buy call on Ingenia. (david.winning@wsj.com; @dwinningWSJ)
